title: Supply Chain Logistics Orchestration
business: Global manufacturing firms managing complex, multi-vendor logistics networks.
problem: Firms struggle with siloed logistics agents—such as regional warehouse managers, freight forwarders, and customs brokers—that cannot communicate directly, leading to manual data entry and delayed shipment visibility.
solution: The A2A Protocol enables these autonomous logistics agents to interoperate by providing a standardized language for discovery and task delegation, allowing a central orchestrator to request status updates or initiate actions across disparate systems without custom point-to-point integrations.
steps: Publish an Agent Card at the .well-known/agent-card.json endpoint for each logistics agent to declare its capabilities.
Configure the central orchestrator to perform agent discovery by fetching these cards to identify available endpoints.
Implement the SendMessage API for synchronous status queries or SendStreamingMessage for real-time shipment tracking updates.
Utilize standard JWT-based authentication to ensure secure, authorized communication between the orchestrator and regional agents.
outcome: A unified, responsive supply chain ecosystem where agents autonomously negotiate and share task results, significantly reducing manual coordination overhead.
limitation: Opaque execution prevents agents from inspecting the internal logic or proprietary tools of their peers; developers must verify system health through declared capabilities and standardized status events rather than direct introspection.

questions.question: In Supply Chain Logistics Orchestration, how does the A2A Protocol resolve the issue of siloed logistics agents?
options: By forcing all agents to use the same underlying framework and vendor.
By providing a standardized language for discovery and task delegation.
By wrapping every agent as a simple, stateless tool for the orchestrator.
By replacing the need for an orchestrator with a decentralized peer-to-peer mesh.
questions.explanation: The solution explicitly states that A2A provides a standardized language for discovery and task delegation to allow agents to interoperate.
questions.evidence: The A2A Protocol enables these autonomous logistics agents to interoperate by providing a standardized language for discovery and task delegation

questions.question: In Supply Chain Logistics Orchestration, what is a primary limitation of the Opaque Execution design principle?
options: It prevents agents from communicating with each other across different networks.
It forces agents to expose their private memory and proprietary tools to peers.
It prevents agents from inspecting the internal logic of their collaborators.
It requires all agents to be hosted on the same physical server to maintain security.
questions.explanation: The limitation section notes that opaque execution prevents agents from seeing the internal logic of their peers, requiring reliance on declared capabilities.
questions.evidence: Opaque execution prevents agents from inspecting the internal logic or proprietary tools of their peers
